preconditions.description: The number of test cases t is an integer between 1 and 1000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(isinstance(n, int) and 1 <= n <= 100 for n in [int(line) for line in stdin_lines[1::2] if line.strip()])
preconditions.description: For each test case, n is an integer between 1 and 100 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(len(row) == n and all(c in '01' for c in row) for row in matrix_rows)
preconditions.description: The binary matrix b consists of n rows, each containing exactly n characters, where each character is either '0' or '1'.
The sum of n over all test cases does not exceed 1000.
It is guaranteed that a valid solution exists for the given input.

postconditions.description: The output contains exactly n lines for each of the t test cases.

postconditions.expression: all(1 <= size <= n and len(elements) == size and all(1 <= x <= n for x in elements) and len(set(elements)) == size for (size, elements) in parsed_output_sets)
postconditions.description: Each output line specifies a nonempty set of distinct integers between 1 and n, with the count matching the number of elements listed.

postconditions.expression: len(set(tuple(sorted(s)) for s in all_sets)) == n
postconditions.description: All n sets constructed for a test case are distinct.

postconditions.expression: all((set(A[i]) < set(A[j])) == (b[i][j] == '1') for i in range(n) for j in range(n))
postconditions.description: For every pair (i, j), b[i][j] is '1' if and only if set A_i is a proper subset of set A_j.
